issues: The first render had the figure missing from 26.2s onward — an SVG transform-origin bug. Caught by sampling the render, not by any still. Fixed and re-verified.

There is a great deal of intentional silence: 2.2s after the errand is taken, 1.6s for the search, 1.0s after the kick and 2.6s on the closing image. It is the design, not a defect — the acting lives there.

atelier.art_direction: Black ink on warm white paper #FCFBF8, the ink-sketch playbook. All structure and the character are ink #333 with a live hand-drawn boil on every stroke. Orange #D4611B is the errand and only the errand; red #C8322B appears once, on the lid seam of the box that will not open; blue #2E6E9E appears once, drawn along the line of closed boxes at the end. Type is Patrick Hand, the full TTF, on HTML overlay divs — the first handwriting this channel has used. The signature device is the doorway itself, drawn as a contraption: a barrier arm hinged on the left upright at exactly hand height, folded flat against the post until it drops to horizontal and sweeps the errand out of the figure's hand. Motion character is the largest departure of the four productions: real human motion capture. The figure walks, creeps, kicks and sits like a person because a person did it; nothing about the acting is authored. The world slides past a fixed figure, so the camera language is one horizontal scroll and one pull-back rather than a cut list — the whole piece is a single shot.

issues: Resolved before render: the actor's facing flip used transformOrigin in px on an SVG <g>. GSAP needs svgOrigin in user units there, and the wrong one threw the whole figure off the page from 26.2s to the end. It is invisible in a still and only showed up on the first full render — the reason this pipeline's compose stage insists on sampling the finished file.

Resolved before render: the sit clip is exactly 6.00s and the segment was 6.60s, so it wrapped and began sitting down again instead of ending on its feet. Fixed with loop:false, which holds the clip's last frame.

Resolved before render: the character had no visible face — the style's white-dot eyes are invisible on an unfilled head on white paper — so the turn at 26.2s did not read at all on a symmetrical stick figure. Two ink eyes and a nose, both on one side, fixed both problems at once.
Accepted: the catalog has no 'stands still, confused' clip, so the search beat is carried by shuffle plus staging. Verified legible on the contact sheet; the library was not extended.
